docs/dev/tmp/review-context-00110-c2.md:56:### Problem Statement
docs/dev/tmp/review-context-00110-c2.md:57:`--dry-run` walks every selected tree to count files and bytes, which is slow on a large tree and shows no table of what a run would do. `_expand_stamp` calls `datetime.now()` per instance (`src/tools/backup/capabilities/tar_archive.py:373`), so two instances started seconds apart can resolve a `%H%M%S` stamp differently, and nothing detects two instances that resolve to the same output file. With outputs replaced by later runs, two instances writing one path silently lose one archive, and under parallel execution they race.

/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:8:
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:9:TDD: write the failing test (RED), make it pass (GREEN), refactor. One behavior per test. No logic in tests. Coverage target 80%, higher on critical paths.
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:10:
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:11:## Rulings
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:12:
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:13:**Mocking**
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:14:- Patch where the name is *used*, not where it's defined: `@patch("myapp.service.requests")`, not `@patch("requests")`.
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:15:- `autospec=True` so the mock rejects calls the real API would reject.
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:16:- Mock at the boundary (I/O, network, clock). Never mock the thing under test.
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:17:- Async: assert with `assert_awaited_once()`, not `assert_called_once()`.
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:18:
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:19:**Fixtures**
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:20:- `yield` for teardown; the line after `yield` is the cleanup.
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:21:- Default to function scope. Widen to `module`/`session` only for genuinely expensive resources.
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:22:- `autouse` hides dependencies — use sparingly; prefer explicit injection.
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:23:- `tmp_path` for temp files (auto-cleanup, `Path` API), not `tempfile`.
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:24:
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:25:**Parametrize**
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:26:- `@pytest.mark.parametrize` over loops — distinct test IDs, filterable with `-k`.
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:27:- Pass `ids=[...]` when params are objects or tuples; pytest already auto-names plain str/int/bool readably.
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:28:
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:29:**Config**
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:30:- One config in `pyproject.toml` (`[tool.pytest.ini_options]`), not a separate `pytest.ini`.
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:31:- `--strict-markers` so a typo'd marker fails instead of silently passing.
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:32:- Register custom markers — e.g. `slow`, `@pytest.mark.unit`, `@pytest.mark.integration` — so `--strict-markers` catches a typo.
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:33:- Coverage locally: `pytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing` — the missing-line report is the point; a bare percentage is not actionable.
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:34:
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:35:**Async (pytest-asyncio)**
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:36:- Default mode is `strict`: an async test with no `@pytest.mark.asyncio` is silently not collected. Set `asyncio_mode = "auto"` in `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` to drop the per-test marker.
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md:37:- Use `@pytest_asyncio.fixture` for async fixtures in strict mode.

/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-patterns/SKILL.md:8:
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-patterns/SKILL.md:9:Pick a side. These are the rulings, not a tutorial.
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-patterns/SKILL.md:10:
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-patterns/SKILL.md:11:## Idioms that earn their place
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-patterns/SKILL.md:12:
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-patterns/SKILL.md:13:| Rule | Why |
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-patterns/SKILL.md:14:|------|-----|
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-patterns/SKILL.md:15:| `X \| Y`, not `Union[X, Y]` | 3.10+ runtime syntax; clearer. On 3.9 it parses only under `from __future__ import annotations` and still breaks `get_type_hints`/`isinstance` — keep `Optional`/`Union` if you support 3.9. |
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-patterns/SKILL.md:16:| `Protocol`, not `ABC`, for duck typing | Structural typing; no inheritance you don't control. |
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-patterns/SKILL.md:17:| `@dataclass(frozen=True)` for immutable records, plain `dataclass` only when you must mutate, `NamedTuple` for lightweight immutable rows | Pydantic only when you need validation. |
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-patterns/SKILL.md:18:| `raise New(...) from e` | Marks the explicit cause. A bare `raise New()` still chains implicitly ("During handling..."); use `from None` to suppress. |
/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-patterns/SKILL.md:19:| `@functools.wraps` on every decorator | Without it the wrapper loses `__name__`, `__doc__`, signature. |

# backup: --plan preview and once-per-run output resolution

Source: `docs/dev/project-management/intake/processed/00107-backup-multi-source-parallel/discovery.md`. Depends on PRD 00109 (skip state, `items`). PRDs 00111 and 00112 depend on this one.

## Overview

### Problem Statement
`--dry-run` walks every selected tree to count files and bytes, which is slow on a large tree and shows no table of what a run would do. `_expand_stamp` calls `datetime.now()` per instance (`src/tools/backup/capabilities/tar_archive.py:373`), so two instances started seconds apart can resolve a `%H%M%S` stamp differently, and nothing detects two instances that resolve to the same output file. With outputs replaced by later runs, two instances writing one path silently lose one archive, and under parallel execution they race.

### Target Users
The solo operator who checks a multi-instance plan before a scheduled run and wants a safe plan every time.

### Success Metrics
- `uv run pytest tests/tools/backup/test_plan.py -q` passes.
- `--plan` performs no recursive walk: `test_plan_does_not_walk_tree` (patches `os.walk` to raise) passes.
- `test_duplicate_outputs_rejected_before_writing` passes: neither colliding instance writes.

## Functional Decomposition

### Capability: Plan preview
Show what a run would do from cheap filesystem checks only.

#### Feature: Capability plan
- **Description**: Each capability can describe one instance without archiving.
- **Inputs**: the same kwargs as `run` (`source`, `out`, `items`, `engine`, `label`, `now`).
- **Outputs**: `PlanEntry(label, source, out, status, reason, replaces)`; `status` is `run`, `skip` or `fail`; `replaces` is true when `out` already exists.
- **Behavior**: `fail` for unknown engine, `out` inside `source`, `items` invalid per PRD 00109, or `source` not a directory; `skip` for a missing `source` (`source not found: <path>`) or when no selected item exists (`lexists`); otherwise `run`. Uses `lexists`/`is_dir`/`stat` only; never `os.walk`.

#### Feature: `--plan` flag
- **Description**: Prints the plan table and exits without writing.
- **Inputs**: `--plan`, plus the usual `--only` and `--tag` selection and the `--source`/`--out` overrides.
- **Outputs**: one `console.info` line per instance: `<label>  <status>  <source> -> <out>` followed by `  (<reason>)` when a reason exists and `  [replaces existing]` when `replaces`; exit 1 if any entry is `fail`, else 0.
- **Behavior**: `--plan` with `--dry-run` fails: `--plan and --dry-run are mutually exclusive` (exit 1). `--dry-run` is unchanged.

### Capability: Output resolution
Resolve each output once and reject collisions.

#### Feature: Run-wide timestamp
- **Description**: One `now` per run feeds every stamp expansion.
- **Inputs**: `now: datetime`.
- **Outputs**: `_expand_stamp(pattern, now)` uses it; when `now` is absent it falls back to `datetime.now()`.
- **Behavior**: `Runner` takes `now = datetime.now()` once per `run`/`plan` call and passes it as a kwarg.

#### Feature: Duplicate output rejection
- **Description**: Two selected instances may not resolve to one output path.
- **Inputs**: plan entries of the selected instances.
- **Outputs**: for each group sharing a resolved `out`, every instance in the group yields `StepResult(name, success=False, message="output '<out>' is also the output of '<other names, comma separated, sorted>'")` and is not executed; the others run.
- **Behavior**: compared as `os.path.normpath` of the expanded path with `~` expanded; applies to `run`, `--dry-run` and `--plan`.

### Repository Structure

src/tools/backup/capabilities/__init__.py    # Maps to: Capability plan (protocol)

AGENTS.md:3:BUVIS gems monorepo. Python toolkit (buvis-pybase + zettel) and CLI tools, shipped as a single PyPI package `buvis-gems`. Supports Python 3.11+.
AGENTS.md:4:
AGENTS.md:5:## Reading these instructions
AGENTS.md:6:
AGENTS.md:7:This root `AGENTS.md` is the always-on canonical guidance. Some directories also
AGENTS.md:8:carry their own nested `AGENTS.md` with rules scoped to the code beside them.
AGENTS.md:9:Before working on files in a directory, discover and read any `AGENTS.md` on the
AGENTS.md:10:path from the repo root down to that directory, and follow it for files in its
AGENTS.md:11:scope. Do this yourself even if your host did not load those files automatically
AGENTS.md:12:— host loading of nested files varies and is not guaranteed (see
AGENTS.md:13:[`docs/dev/architecture/agent-host-support.md`](docs/dev/architecture/agent-host-support.md)).
AGENTS.md:14:
AGENTS.md:15:## Quick Start
AGENTS.md:16:
AGENTS.md:17:```bash
AGENTS.md:18:uv sync --all-groups --all-extras            # install deps
AGENTS.md:19:pre-commit install                          # setup hooks
AGENTS.md:20:uv run pytest                               # run tests
AGENTS.md:21:uv run pytest -m snapshot                   # run snapshot tests only (skipped off canonical env)
AGENTS.md:22:uv run pytest --snapshot-update             # regenerate snapshot baselines (local use only)
AGENTS.md:23:uv run mypy src/lib/ src/tools/              # type check
AGENTS.md:24:uv run sphinx-build -b html docs/source docs/build/html  # build docs
AGENTS.md:25:```
AGENTS.md:26:
AGENTS.md:27:## Architecture
AGENTS.md:28:
AGENTS.md:29:```text
AGENTS.md:30:src/
AGENTS.md:31:├── lib/buvis/pybase/           # shared library (namespace pkg: no buvis/__init__.py)
AGENTS.md:32:│   ├── adapters/               # jira, console, config adapters
AGENTS.md:33:│   ├── configuration/          # settings/config helpers
AGENTS.md:34:│   ├── filesystem/             # file utilities
AGENTS.md:35:│   ├── formatting/             # output formatting
AGENTS.md:36:│   └── zettel/                 # zettel subsystem
AGENTS.md:37:│       ├── domain/             # entities, services, interfaces, value objects
AGENTS.md:38:│       ├── application/        # use cases
AGENTS.md:39:│       ├── infrastructure/     # formatters, repositories, file parsers
AGENTS.md:40:│       └── integrations/       # jira assemblers
AGENTS.md:41:└── tools/
AGENTS.md:42:    ├── bim/                    # BUVIS InfoMesh CLI (zettel integration)
AGENTS.md:43:    ├── dot/                    # dotfiles manager
AGENTS.md:44:    ├── fctracker/              # foreign currency tracker
AGENTS.md:45:    ├── fren/                   # file renamer toolkit
AGENTS.md:46:    ├── morph/                  # file conversion toolkit
AGENTS.md:47:    ├── muc/                    # music collection tools
AGENTS.md:48:    ├── netscan/                # network scanning tools
AGENTS.md:49:    ├── outlookctl/             # Outlook CLI
AGENTS.md:50:    ├── pinger/                 # ICMP ping utilities
AGENTS.md:51:    ├── puc/                    # photo utility collection
AGENTS.md:52:    ├── readerctl/              # Readwise Reader CLI
AGENTS.md:53:    ├── sysup/                  # system update tools
AGENTS.md:54:    ├── vuc/                    # video utility collection
AGENTS.md:55:    └── zseq/                   # Zettelsequence utilities
AGENTS.md:56:tests/
AGENTS.md:57:├── lib/                        # library tests
AGENTS.md:58:│   ├── pybase/
AGENTS.md:59:│   ├── zettel/
AGENTS.md:60:│   └── zettel_integrations/
AGENTS.md:61:└── tools/                      # CLI tool tests
AGENTS.md:62:tools/                          # Dev command shims (on PATH via mise) + helpers
AGENTS.md:63:├── release                     # public shim → mise `release` task
AGENTS.md:64:└── lib/                        # helpers, invoked by path (NOT on PATH)
AGENTS.md:65:    ├── release                 # release impl: bump+tag+push
AGENTS.md:66:    ├── pin_deps.py             # pin deps from uv.lock for publishing
AGENTS.md:67:    ├── scaffold.py             # scaffold a new tool
AGENTS.md:68:    ├── check_audit_ignores.py  # pip-audit suppression guard (+ audit/ config)
AGENTS.md:69:    ├── check_tool_wiring.py    # pre-commit tool-wiring check
AGENTS.md:70:    ├── parity_brief_portfolio.py

AGENTS.md:73:
AGENTS.md:74:**Key patterns:**
AGENTS.md:75:
AGENTS.md:76:- **Single package**: `buvis-gems` on PyPI, one `uv tool install`
AGENTS.md:77:- **Namespace package**: `src/lib/buvis/` has no `__init__.py`
AGENTS.md:78:- **Hatch packages**: each `src/tools/<name>/` maps to top-level `<name>` in wheel
AGENTS.md:79:- **Libraries are internal**: pybase + zettel not published separately
AGENTS.md:80:- **All-interface rule**: every command/action must work across CLI, TUI, API, and WebUI
AGENTS.md:81:
AGENTS.md:82:## Tool Structure
AGENTS.md:83:
AGENTS.md:84:Every tool under `src/tools/<name>/` follows a base layout:
AGENTS.md:85:
AGENTS.md:86:```text
AGENTS.md:87:tool_name/
AGENTS.md:88:├── __init__.py
AGENTS.md:89:├── __main__.py
AGENTS.md:90:├── cli.py              # Click entry point
AGENTS.md:91:├── settings.py         # Tool-specific settings
AGENTS.md:92:└── commands/           # One module per CLI command
AGENTS.md:93:```
AGENTS.md:94:
AGENTS.md:95:Add subdirs only when needed:
AGENTS.md:96:
AGENTS.md:97:| Dir | When | Example |
AGENTS.md:98:|-----|------|---------|
AGENTS.md:99:| `adapters/` | External service clients | fctracker, readerctl |
AGENTS.md:100:| `domain/` | Business logic beyond simple commands | fctracker |
AGENTS.md:101:| `shared/` | Code reused across commands | zseq |
AGENTS.md:102:
AGENTS.md:103:> `bim/commands/serve/frontend/` contains the WebUI SvelteKit app — the only tool with a frontend subtree.
AGENTS.md:104:
AGENTS.md:105:> `bim/commands/doc/` follows the existing `commands/serve/`-style group pattern with a `shared/` subdir holding cross-command utilities (pipeline, OCR/classifier/extractor adapters, state DB, issuer registry, zettel writer).
AGENTS.md:106:
AGENTS.md:107:## Code Conventions
AGENTS.md:108:
AGENTS.md:109:**Type hints** — modern style, no `Optional`:
AGENTS.md:110:
AGENTS.md:111:```python
AGENTS.md:112:from __future__ import annotations
AGENTS.md:113:def foo(path: Path | None = None) -> list[str]: ...
AGENTS.md:114:```
AGENTS.md:115:
AGENTS.md:116:**Imports**:
AGENTS.md:117:
AGENTS.md:118:- Explicit `__all__` in `__init__.py`
AGENTS.md:119:- `TYPE_CHECKING` guards for type-only imports
AGENTS.md:120:
AGENTS.md:121:**Docstrings**: Google format
AGENTS.md:122:
AGENTS.md:123:**CLI pattern**: Click-based. `buvis_options` adds `--version`, `--config`, `--log-level`, `--debug`, and `--update` to every tool automatically:
AGENTS.md:124:
AGENTS.md:125:```python
AGENTS.md:126:@click.command()
AGENTS.md:127:@buvis_options
AGENTS.md:128:@click.pass_context
AGENTS.md:129:def cli(ctx: click.Context) -> None:
AGENTS.md:130:    settings = get_settings(ctx)
AGENTS.md:131:    ...
AGENTS.md:132:```
AGENTS.md:133:
AGENTS.md:134:**Lazy imports in CLI handlers**: import command classes inside handler functions, not at module level. This avoids pulling in optional/heavy dependencies before the user picks a subcommand:
AGENTS.md:135:
AGENTS.md:136:```python
AGENTS.md:137:@cli.command("create")
AGENTS.md:138:@click.pass_context
AGENTS.md:139:def create(ctx):
AGENTS.md:140:    from bim.commands.create_note.create_note import CommandCreateNote
AGENTS.md:141:    ...
AGENTS.md:142:```
AGENTS.md:143:
AGENTS.md:144:## Error Handling
AGENTS.md:145:
AGENTS.md:146:**Command layer** (`commands/`):
AGENTS.md:147:- Return `CommandResult` for all outcomes — success and failure
AGENTS.md:148:- Catch expected exceptions (e.g. `FileNotFoundError`) internally, return `CommandResult(success=False, error=str(exc))`
AGENTS.md:149:- No `console.panic()` or `sys.exit()` inside command classes
AGENTS.md:150:- No custom exception classes for control flow
AGENTS.md:151:
AGENTS.md:152:**CLI layer** (`cli.py`):
AGENTS.md:153:- Inspect `CommandResult` and call `console.panic()` / `console.failure()` / `console.success()`
AGENTS.md:154:- Use `console.report_result()` for standardized output
AGENTS.md:155:- Catch `ImportError` for optional deps, call `console.require_import()`
AGENTS.md:156:- Catch `FatalError` for unrecoverable infrastructure failures
AGENTS.md:157:
AGENTS.md:158:**Click argument validation**:
AGENTS.md:159:- Avoid parse-time validators that short-circuit before the callback (`click.Path(exists=True)`, `IntRange`, custom `ParamType.convert` that raises). They emit Click's default `Usage: ... Error: ...` formatting and bypass the buvis console.
AGENTS.md:160:- Validate inside the callback instead: `if not path.is_file(): console.panic(f"file not found: {path}"); return`.
AGENTS.md:161:- `click.Choice` is the exception — its parse-time error lists the valid values, which is more useful than a rewritten message.
AGENTS.md:162:
AGENTS.md:163:**Console methods**:
AGENTS.md:164:- Fatal (exit): `console.panic(msg)` — prints + exits with code 1
AGENTS.md:165:- Recoverable: `console.failure(msg)` — prints, continues
AGENTS.md:166:- Status: `console.success()`, `console.warning()`, `console.info()`
AGENTS.md:167:- All user-facing output must route through `console`. No `print()`, `sys.stdout.write()`, `sys.stderr.write()`, `click.echo()`, `click.secho()`, or the Python logging module. Plain writes bypass the buvis prefix markers (`✘`, `✓`, etc.) and become indistinguishable from stray output, which is what makes a missed `console.panic` look like a print statement to the user.
AGENTS.md:168:- The one sanctioned exception is the `dot filter` clean/smudge plumbing, which writes git's blob payload as raw bytes on stdout and at most one error line on stderr, because git owns both streams and a console marker would corrupt the payload (discovery R12).
AGENTS.md:169:- Never let raw exceptions (stack traces) reach the user.

AGENTS.md:171:## Invariants (evolution guardrails)
AGENTS.md:172:
AGENTS.md:173:These encode the failure classes surfaced by the 2026-07-09 evolution assessment (`docs/dev/project-management/reviews/evolution-assessment-2026-07-09.md`). Each is either **HOLDS** (enforce it) or a **GAP** (a tracked PRD is closing it — write new code to the target state, not the current one).
AGENTS.md:174:
AGENTS.md:175:- **Atomic persistence** — never persist a note, state file, or config with a bare `Path.write_text`/`open(...,"w")`. Use `pybase.filesystem.atomic_write` (tempfile + fsync + `os.replace`). Truncate-then-write loses data on crash/ENOSPC. *HOLDS for the library and note/updater write paths (00041) — keep it, except `ConfigWriter.write` (`configuration/config_writer.py`), which still does a bare `write_text` — deliberately out of scope for 00041. GAP → pidash was closed by retiring pidash (00071); autopilot-state durability now lives in the buvis home repo (tracon/statectl), not gems.*
AGENTS.md:176:- **Confine request-derived paths** — any filesystem path built from an HTTP request / external input must be `resolve()`d and asserted under an allowed root before read/write/delete/open. Network-facing servers must have auth + `TrustedHostMiddleware`. *HOLDS (00042) — bim serve confines request paths via `confine_path` (403 outside the vault/archive roots), mints a startup token required as `X-Buvis-Token`, installs `TrustedHostMiddleware`, and warns on a non-loopback bind (`commands/serve/_security.py`). Keep it.*
AGENTS.md:177:- **The library stays interface-agnostic** — `src/lib/buvis/pybase/` must not import a UI framework at module import time or emit output outside the console adapter. No import-time Click monkey-patching, no `sys.exit`/`click.echo`/`print` in lib code. A TUI/API/WebUI process must be able to `import` settings without pulling Click. *HOLDS (00052) — keep it.*
AGENTS.md:178:- **One action, one implementation across interfaces** — CLI/TUI/API/WebUI adapters must drive the same command class / use case through the composition root and return `CommandResult`; do not reimplement business logic per interface (dot's TUI is the anti-pattern; bim's serve action registry is the exemplar). *HOLDS (00051 design → 00053/00054) — the all-interface seam design (00051) is realized: dot's git ops unified behind `DotGitService` (00053) and bim's serve/TUI converged on the shared action registry (00054). Keep it.*
AGENTS.md:179:- **Claim/lifecycle release on any exit** — resource claims and locks release in `finally` (or catch `BaseException`), never only `except Exception`; `KeyboardInterrupt` must not leak a claim. *HOLDS (00044) — the bim doc claim/dedup pipeline releases claims and locks in `finally` (`commands/doc/shared/`); keep it.*
AGENTS.md:180:- **`CommandResult` discipline** — commands return `CommandResult`; the CLI/adapter layer renders it (`console.report_result`) and maps exit/HTTP status. No `sys.exit`/`console.panic` inside command classes. *HOLDS in `src/tools/*/commands/**` — keep it.*
AGENTS.md:181:- **Clean-architecture layering + tool isolation** — zettel `domain → application → infrastructure → integrations` one-directional; no cross-tool imports; no `src/lib → src/tools`. *HOLDS — keep it.*
AGENTS.md:182:
AGENTS.md:183:## Testing
AGENTS.md:184:
AGENTS.md:185:- pytest + pytest-mock + pytest-cov
AGENTS.md:186:- Tests in `tests/` mirror `src/lib/` and `src/tools/` structure
AGENTS.md:187:- Mock subprocess calls heavily
AGENTS.md:188:- Class-based test organization
AGENTS.md:189:- **No unused imports/variables**
AGENTS.md:190:- **Markers**: `pytest -m <tool>` runs one tool, `pytest -m lib` runs library tests, `pytest -m "not bim"` excludes a tool. Auto-applied by path in `tests/conftest.py` — no decorators needed. Scaffold registers markers for new tools.
AGENTS.md:191:- **Snapshot tests** (`@pytest.mark.snapshot`) only run on the canonical env (Linux + Python 3.12) — SVG output from Rich/Textual differs across OS/Python so baselines must come from one place. Anywhere else they are auto-skipped. To regenerate baselines run the `update-snapshots` GitHub workflow (`gh workflow run update-snapshots.yml`); it runs `pytest --snapshot-update` on the canonical env and commits the result. Force locally with `BUVIS_SNAPSHOT_CANONICAL=1` only if you know what you're doing.

With outputs replaced by later runs, two instances writing one path silently lose one archive, and under parallel execution they

+def test_cli_plan_prints_real_config_without_creating_archive(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    source = tmp_path / "notes"
+    source.mkdir()
+    out = tmp_path / "notes.tar.gz"
+    config = tmp_path / "backup.yaml"
+    config.write_text(
+        json.dumps(
+            {
+                "instances": {

+        encoding="utf-8",

+    result = CliRunner().invoke(cli, ["--config-dir", str(tmp_path), "--config", str(config), "--plan"])

+    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output

+    instances = {}
+    for name in ("notes", "notes-copy"):
+        source = tmp_path / name

+        instances[name] = {"use": "tar-archive", "with": {"source": str(source), "out": str(out)}}
+    cfg = BackupConfig.model_validate({"instances": instances})
+
+    results = list(Runner(cfg, dry_run=dry_run).run(list(cfg.instances.items())))
+
+    assert len(results) == 2
+    assert {result.label for result in results} == {"notes", "notes-copy"}
+    for result in results:

+        assert result.success is False
+        assert result.message == f"output '{out}' is also the output of '{other}'"
+    assert out.exists() is existing

+def _config(tmp_path: Path, instances: dict[str, dict[str, object]]) -> Path:
+    path = tmp_path / "backup.yaml"
+    isolated = {"git-src": {"use": "tar-archive", "enabled": False}, **instances}
+    path.write_text(json.dumps({"instances": isolated}), encoding="utf-8")
+    return path
+

+def _instance(source: Path, out: Path, **fields: object) -> dict[str, object]:
+    return {"use": "tar-archive", "with": {"source": str(source), "out": str(out)}, **fields}

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", ["notes", "photos"])

+def test_cli_plan_formats_run_and_skip_rows_and_preserves_existing_outputs(
+    tmp_path: Path,
+    name: str,
+    existing: bool,
+) -> None:
+    source = tmp_path / name
+    source.mkdir()
+    missing = tmp_path / f"{name}-missing"
+    out = tmp_path / f"{name}.tgz"
+    missing_out = tmp_path / f"{name}-missing.tgz"
+    if existing:
+        out.write_bytes(b"original archive")
+        missing_out.write_bytes(b"original missing-source archive")
+    config = _config(
+        tmp_path,
+        {
+            name: _instance(source, out),
+            f"{name}-missing": _instance(missing, missing_out),
+        },
+    )
+    suffix = "  [replaces existing]" if existing else ""
+
+    with patch("backup.cli.console.info", autospec=True) as info:
+        result = CliRunner().invoke(cli, ["--config-dir", str(tmp_path), "--config", str(config), "--plan"])
+
+    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
+    assert [call.args[0] for call in info.call_args_list] == [
+        f"{name}  run  {source} -> {out}{suffix}",
+        f"{name}-missing  skip  {missing} -> {missing_out}  (source not found: {missing}){suffix}",
+    ]
+    assert not missing.exists()
+    assert out.exists() is existing
+    assert missing_out.exists() is existing
+    if existing:
+        assert out.read_bytes() == b"original archive"
+        assert missing_out.read_bytes() == b"original missing-source archive"

+def _source(root: Path, name: str) -> Path:
+    source = root / name
+    source.mkdir(parents=True)
+    (source / "tiny.txt").write_bytes(name.encode())
+    (source / "tiny.txt-copy").write_bytes(f"{name}-copy".encode())
+    return source
+
+
+def _invoke(interface: str, mode: str, values: dict[str, object]) -> list[PlanEntry | StepResult]:
+    if interface == "capability":
+        archive = TarArchive()
+        if mode == "plan":
+            return [archive.plan(label="selected", **values)]
+        return list(archive.run(label="selected", dry_run=mode == "dry-run", **values))
+    cfg = BackupConfig.model_validate({"instances": {"selected": {"use": "tar-archive", "with": values}}})
+    runner = Runner(cfg, dry_run=mode == "dry-run")
+    selected = list(cfg.instances.items())
+    return runner.plan(selected) if mode == "plan" else list(runner.run(selected))
+
+
+def _assert_archive(out: Path, name: str) -> None:
+    with tarfile.open(out, "r:gz") as archive:
+        files = {member.name for member in archive.getmembers() if member.isfile()}
+        assert files == {f"{name}/tiny.txt", f"{name}/tiny.txt-copy"}
+        for filename, payload in (("tiny.txt", name), ("tiny.txt-copy", f"{name}-copy")):
+            member = archive.extractfile(f"{name}/{filename}")
+            assert member is not None
+            assert member.read() == payload.encode()
+
+
+def _snapshot(root: Path) -> dict[str, bytes | None]:
+    return {str(path.relative_to(root)): path.read_bytes() if path.is_file() else None for path in root.rglob("*")}
+
+

+    values = {"source": str(source), "out": str(out)}
+    omitted = _invoke(interface, "plan", values)
+    results = _invoke(interface, mode, {**values, "engine": ""})
+
+    assert len(omitted) == len(results) == 1
+    assert omitted[0].status == "run"
+    result = results[0]
+    assert result.label == "selected"
+    if mode == "plan":
+        assert result == omitted[0]
+        assert result.source == str(source)
+        assert result.out == str(out)
+        assert result.replaces is False
+    else:
+        assert result.success is True
+        assert result.skipped is False
+        assert result.out_path == str(out)
+    assert out.exists() is (mode == "run")
+    assert out.parent.exists() is (mode == "run")
+    if mode == "run":
+        _assert_archive(out, name)
+    assert (source / "tiny.txt").read_bytes() == name.encode()

# Backup's own top-level config keys. The shared config stack (config.yaml /
# buvis.yaml) carries other tools' and global fields; only these are projected
# into BackupConfig, whose extra="forbid" would otherwise reject them.
_BACKUP_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS = frozenset({"instances", "excludes"})


def _is_backup_specific(path: Path) -> bool:
    """Whether ``path`` is a backup-specific config file (``buvis-backup*.yaml``).

    A backup-specific file should carry only backup's own keys, so an unknown
    top-level key in it is a typo. A shared file (``config.yaml`` / ``buvis.yaml``)
    legitimately carries other tools' + global keys and is not checked.
    """
    return path.name.startswith("buvis-backup")


def _unknown_top_level_keys(data: dict[str, object]) -> set[str]:
    """Return top-level keys in ``data`` that are not backup's.

    A list key may carry a ``+`` / ``-`` directive suffix (``excludes+`` /
    ``excludes-``, PRD 00080), so the suffix is stripped before the membership
    check. Non-mapping documents contribute nothing.
    """
    unknown: set[str] = set()
    for key in data:
        base = key[:-1] if key.endswith(("+", "-")) else key
        if base not in _BACKUP_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS:
            unknown.add(key)
    return unknown

    exclude_add: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    exclude_remove: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    with_: dict[str, object] = Field(default_factory=dict, alias="with")


class BackupConfig(BaseModel):
    """The whole merged, validated backup configuration.

    ``instances`` is a name-keyed map of capability instances; ``excludes`` is
    the global basename exclude list that layers via 00080's ``excludes+`` /
    ``excludes-`` directives across gem -> user -> machine config.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True)

    instances: dict[str, BackupInstance] = {}
    excludes: tuple[str, ...] = ()


def effective_excludes(cfg: BackupConfig, instance: BackupInstance) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Resolve inherited excludes, exact removals, then additions in order."""
    inherited = cfg.excludes if instance.inherit_excludes else ()
    remaining = (pattern for pattern in inherited if pattern not in instance.exclude_remove)
    return tuple(dict.fromkeys((*remaining, *instance.exclude_add)))


def _validate_capabilities(cfg: BackupConfig) -> None:
    """Reject unknown ``use:`` names and unknown ``with:`` inputs.

    Raises:
        FatalError: on an unknown capability name or an unknown ``with:`` input
            for a known capability.
    """
    for name, instance in cfg.instances.items():
        capability = CAPABILITIES.get(instance.use)
        if capability is None:
            msg = f"instance '{name}': unknown capability '{instance.use}'"
            raise FatalError(msg)
        accepted = set(capability.inputs)
        unknown = set(instance.with_) - accepted
        if unknown:
            allowed = ", ".join(sorted(accepted)) or "(none)"
            msg = (
                f"instance '{name}': capability '{instance.use}' got unknown "
                f"input(s) {', '.join(sorted(unknown))}; accepted: {allowed}"
            )
            raise FatalError(msg)


def _load_default() -> dict[str, object]:
    """Load the bundled ``default.yaml`` as the lowest-priority layer.

    Anchored to this module's own file rather than resolved by package name:
    under pytest's importlib mode the ``backup`` name is a namespace shared with
    the test package, so ``importlib.resources.files("backup")`` can resolve to
    the wrong path entry. ``default.yaml`` always ships beside this module in the
    wheel (hatch packages the whole ``backup`` directory), so its own directory
    is the unambiguous anchor.

    Loaded through :meth:`ConfigurationLoader.load_yaml` — the SAME
    env-substituting loader the user layers use — so ``${HOME}`` (and the
    ``${VAR:-default}`` / ``$${VAR}`` escape forms) in the bundled defaults
    expand identically to user config. ``Path.expanduser`` only expands ``~``, so
    a raw ``yaml.safe_load`` would leave the zero-config source as a literal
    ``${HOME}/git/src``. ``load_yaml`` raises ``MissingEnvVarError`` /
    ``yaml.YAMLError`` for a missing required var / bad YAML; ``load_config``
    wraps those to :class:`FatalError`, and returns ``{}`` for an empty file.
    """
    resource = Path(__file__).with_name(_DEFAULT_CONFIG_RESOURCE)
    return ConfigurationLoader.load_yaml(resource)


def load_config(config_dir: str | None = None, config_path: str | None = None) -> BackupConfig:
    """Merge the bundled default with user config files and validate.

    Layers, lowest priority first: the bundled ``default.yaml``, then the user
    files returned by :meth:`ConfigurationLoader.find_config_files_ranked`
    (already low-to-high — never reverse it). An explicit ``config_path`` (from
    ``--config FILE``) is the single highest-priority layer, above every
    discovered file. Merged via :meth:`ConfigurationLoader.merge_configs` (later
    wins, ``excludes+`` / ``excludes-`` directives applied), validated against
    :class:`BackupConfig`, and finally checked for unknown capability names /
    inputs.

    Args:
        config_dir: Explicit config directory (from ``--config-dir``), threaded
            from the CLI so the tool plan is discovered under the SAME directory
            the settings were resolved from.
        config_path: Explicit config file (from ``--config``), threaded from the
            CLI so ``backup --config FILE`` runs the plan from FILE rather than
            the default locations.

    Raises:
        FatalError: on malformed YAML in a config file, a merge/directive error,
            a missing required env var, an invalid schema, an unknown capability,
            or an unknown ``with:`` input — every failure the CLI's ``FatalError``
            handler can render, never a raw traceback.
    """
    layers: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    try:
        layers.append(_load_default())
    except (yaml.YAMLError, MissingEnvVarError, OSError, UnicodeError) as exc:
        msg = f"failed to load bundled default configuration: {exc}"
        raise FatalError(msg) from exc
    ranked_files: list[Path] = ConfigurationLoader.find_config_files_ranked(
        "backup", config_dir=config_dir, config_path=config_path
    )
    for path in ranked_files:
        try:
            data = ConfigurationLoader.load_yaml(path)
        except (yaml.YAMLError, MissingEnvVarError, OSError, UnicodeError) as exc:
            msg = f"failed to load config file {path}: {exc}"
            raise FatalError(msg) from exc
        # A backup-SPECIFIC file (buvis-backup*.yaml) should carry only backup's
        # keys, so an unknown top-level key there is a typo (instnaces:, exclude:)
        # to reject — the projection below would otherwise silently drop it and
        # run the bundled plan. A SHARED file (config.yaml / buvis.yaml) legitimately
        # carries other tools' + global keys, so its extras are tolerated.
        if _is_backup_specific(path):
            unknown = _unknown_top_level_keys(data)
            if unknown:
                allowed = ", ".join(sorted(_BACKUP_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS))
                msg = (
                    f"unknown key(s) in {path}: {', '.join(sorted(unknown))}; "
                    f"backup config accepts only: {allowed} (with +/- directive suffixes on list keys)"
                )
                raise FatalError(msg)
        layers.append(data)

    try:
        merged = ConfigurationLoader.merge_configs(*layers, known_keys={"excludes"})
    except (ConfigurationError, yaml.YAMLError, MissingEnvVarError) as exc:
        msg = f"failed to merge backup configuration: {exc}"
        raise FatalError(msg) from exc

    # find_config_files_ranked also returns the SHARED config.yaml / buvis.yaml
    # layers, whose global fields (debug, log_level, ...) are not backup's. Project
    # the merged document onto backup's own top-level keys before validation, so a
    # standard global config no longer trips BackupConfig's extra="forbid". Typos in
    # a backup-SPECIFIC file are already rejected above; a typo nested under
    # instances/excludes is caught by the per-instance extra="forbid" and
    # _validate_capabilities.
    backup_config = {key: value for key, value in merged.items() if key in _BACKUP_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS}

    try:
        cfg = BackupConfig.model_validate(backup_config)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        msg = f"invalid backup configuration: {exc}"
        raise FatalError(msg) from exc

    _validate_capabilities(cfg)
    return cfg


def applicable_instances(cfg: BackupConfig) -> list[tuple[str, BackupInstance]]:
    """Return enabled instances sorted by ``(order, name)``."""
    applicable = [(name, inst) for name, inst in cfg.instances.items() if inst.enabled]
    applicable.sort(key=lambda item: (item[1].order, item[0]))
    return applicable

__all__ = ["TarArchive", "WalkResult"]

_ARCHIVE_MODE = 0o600
_ENGINE_PYTHON = "python-tarfile"
_ENGINE_SYSTEM_TAR = "system-tar"


class WalkResult:
    """The outcome of walking + filtering a source tree, before any archive.

    ``files`` is the ordered list of archive MEMBERS as absolute paths:
    surviving directories first (parent-first, so a restore recreates the tree
    including empty dirs), then regular files, then symlinks (each archived as
    the link itself, not followed, matching the former tar backup). ``file_count``
    counts only the regular files (not dirs or symlinks) and ``total_bytes`` sums
    their input sizes (a symlink/dir contributes 0). ``applied`` lists the
    ``.bkpignore`` rules that fired anywhere in the tree (for dry-run reporting).
    """

    def __init__(
        self: WalkResult,
        files: list[Path],
        total_bytes: int,
        applied: list[str],
        file_count: int,
    ) -> None:
        self.files = files
        self.total_bytes = total_bytes
        self.applied = applied
        self._file_count = file_count

    @property
    def file_count(self: WalkResult) -> int:
        return self._file_count


class TarArchive:
    """Tar a source tree into a compressed, ``chmod 600``, atomically-written archive.

    File selection is owned here: it :func:`os.walk`s ``source`` top-down,
    layering each directory's ``.bkpignore`` rules onto the exclude state
    inherited from its ancestors (so ``!target`` un-ignores are path-scoped to
    the file's own subtree), and adds surviving files to a
    ``tarfile.open(mode="w:gz")``. The archive is streamed to a sibling temp
    file, ``fsync``ed, ``chmod 600``ed, then ``os.replace``d into ``out`` — so a
    crash or ENOSPC never leaves a partial ``.tar.gz`` at the final path.
    """

    @property
    def inputs(self: TarArchive) -> Mapping[str, object]:
        return {"source": "", "out": "", "engine": _ENGINE_PYTHON, "items": None}

    def plan(self: TarArchive, **kwargs: object) -> PlanEntry:
        label, engine, source_raw, out_raw, now = _parse_inputs(kwargs)
        message = _missing_input(source_raw, out_raw)
        if message:
            source_text = str(os.path.normpath(Path(source_raw).expanduser())) if source_raw else ""
            out_text = _expand_stamp(out_raw, now) if out_raw else ""
            return PlanEntry(label, source_text, out_text, "fail", message, False)
        source, out = _resolve_paths(source_raw, out_raw, now)
        replaces = out.exists()
        status = "run"
        reason = ""

        if engine not in (_ENGINE_PYTHON, _ENGINE_SYSTEM_TAR):
            status = "fail"
            reason = f"unknown engine '{engine}'; expected {_ENGINE_PYTHON} or {_ENGINE_SYSTEM_TAR}"
        elif not source.is_dir():
            missing = not source.exists()
            status = "skip" if missing else "fail"
            reason = f"{'source not found' if missing else 'source is not a directory'}: {source}"
        else:
            containment = _reject_out_inside_source(label, source, out)
            if containment is not None:
                status = "fail"
                reason = containment.message
            elif "items" in kwargs:
                try:
                    selected = _normalize_items(source, _as_str_tuple(kwargs["items"]))
                except ValueError as exc:
                    status = "fail"
                    reason = str(exc)
                else:
                    if not any(os.path.lexists(source / item) for item in selected):
                        status = "skip"
                        reason = "no selected items to archive"

        return PlanEntry(label, str(source), str(out), status, reason, replaces)

    def run(self: TarArchive, **kwargs: object) -> Iterator[StepResult]:
        label, engine, source_raw, out_raw, now = _parse_inputs(kwargs)
        message = _missing_input(source_raw, out_raw)
        if message:
            yield StepResult(label, success=False, message=message)
            return

        source, out = _resolve_paths(source_raw, out_raw, now)

        if engine not in (_ENGINE_PYTHON, _ENGINE_SYSTEM_TAR):
            yield StepResult(
                label,
                success=False,
                message=f"unknown engine '{engine}'; expected {_ENGINE_PYTHON} or {_ENGINE_SYSTEM_TAR}",
            )
            return

        if not source.is_dir():
            missing_source = not source.exists()
            reason = "source not found" if missing_source else "source is not a directory"
            yield StepResult(label, success=missing_source, message=f"{reason}: {source}", skipped=missing_source)
            return

        containment = _reject_out_inside_source(label, source, out)
        if containment is not None:
            yield containment
            return

        yield from self._run_validated(label, engine, source, out, kwargs)

    def _run_validated(
        self: TarArchive,
        label: str,
        engine: str,
        source: Path,
        out: Path,
        kwargs: dict[str, object],
    ) -> Iterator[StepResult]:
        dry_run = bool(kwargs.get("dry_run", False))
        base_state = ExcludeState(base_excludes=frozenset(_as_str_tuple(kwargs.get("excludes", ()))))
        missing: list[str] = []
        bundle = "items" in kwargs
        if bundle:
            try:
                selected = _normalize_items(source, _as_str_tuple(kwargs["items"]))
            except ValueError as exc:
                yield StepResult(label, success=False, message=str(exc))
                return
            walk, missing = _select_items(source, base_state, selected)
            if not walk.files:
                message = "no selected items to archive"
                if missing:
                    message += f"; missing items: {', '.join(missing)}"
                yield StepResult(label, success=True, message=message, skipped=True)
                return
        else:
            walk = _walk_tree(source, base_state)

        if dry_run:
            result = self._dry_run_result(label, out, walk)
        else:
            result = self._archive_result(label, source if bundle else source.parent, out, walk, engine)
        if missing:
            result.message += f"; missing items: {', '.join(missing)}"
        yield result

    @staticmethod
    def _dry_run_result(label: str, out: Path, walk: WalkResult) -> StepResult:
        applied = ", ".join(walk.applied) if walk.applied else "none"
        message = (
            f"would archive {walk.file_count} files ({walk.total_bytes} bytes) "
            f"-> {out}; .bkpignore rules applied: {applied}"
        )
        return StepResult(
            label,
            success=True,
            message=message,
            archive=ArchiveMeta(out_path=str(out), file_count=walk.file_count, total_bytes=walk.total_bytes),
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _archive_result(label: str, arcbase: Path, out: Path, walk: WalkResult, engine: str) -> StepResult:
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        note = ""
        if engine == _ENGINE_SYSTEM_TAR:
            fallback = _write_archive_system_tar(out, arcbase, walk.files)
            if fallback is not None:
                _write_archive(out, arcbase, walk.files)
                note = f" (system-tar unavailable: {fallback}; used python engine)"
        else:
            _write_archive(out, arcbase, walk.files)
        size = out.stat().st_size
        return StepResult(
            label,
            success=True,
            message=(
                f"archived {walk.file_count} files -> {out} ({walk.total_bytes} bytes in, {size} bytes on disk){note}"
            ),
            archive=ArchiveMeta(out_path=str(out), file_count=walk.file_count, total_bytes=walk.total_bytes),
        )


def _reject_out_inside_source(label: str, source: Path, out: Path) -> StepResult | None:
    """Reject an ``out`` path that lands inside the ``source`` tree.

    An ``out`` under ``source`` makes each run re-archive the previous run's
    archive (unbounded recursive growth). ``out`` may not exist yet, so its
    PARENT is resolved (which does exist — a stamp only expands the basename) and
    the name rejoined, giving a real absolute path to test for containment
    against the resolved source. Returns a failed :class:`StepResult` when ``out``
    is inside ``source`` (the caller yields it and returns before walking),
    otherwise ``None``.
    """
    source_resolved = source.resolve()
    out_resolved = out.parent.resolve() / out.name
    if out_resolved == source_resolved or source_resolved in out_resolved.parents:
        return StepResult(
            label,
            success=False,
            message=(f"out path {out} is inside source {source}; choose an out path outside the backup source"),
        )
    return None


def _normalize_items(source: Path, items: tuple[str, ...]) -> list[Path]:
    """Validate literal item paths and remove duplicate selected subtrees."""
    if not items:
        raise ValueError("items must not be empty")
    selected: list[Path] = []
    for item in items:
        relative = Path(os.path.normpath(item))
        if not item or relative.is_absolute() or relative == Path(".") or relative.parts[0].startswith(".."):
            raise ValueError(f"invalid item '{item}': must be a relative path inside the source")
        for parent in reversed(relative.parents):
            if parent != Path(".") and (source / parent).is_symlink():
                raise ValueError(f"item '{item}' passes through symlink '{parent.as_posix()}'")
        if relative not in selected and not any(parent in selected for parent in relative.parents):
            selected = [path for path in selected if relative not in path.parents]
            selected.append(relative)
    return selected


def _select_items(source: Path, base_state: ExcludeState, selected: list[Path]) -> tuple[WalkResult, list[str]]:
    """Select bundle members using source-relative excludes and ancestor rules."""
    files: list[Path] = []
    missing: list[str] = []
    total_bytes = file_count = 0
    states: dict[str, ExcludeState] = {str(source): state_for_directory(source, base_state)}
    applied: list[str] = []
    for relative in selected:
        path = source / relative
        if not os.path.lexists(path):
            missing.append(relative.as_posix())
            continue
        metadata = path.lstat()
        state = states[str(source)]
        for index, component in enumerate(relative.parts):
            ancestor = source.joinpath(*relative.parts[: index + 1])
            relpath = ancestor.relative_to(source).as_posix()
            if state.is_excluded(component, relpath):
                break
            if index < len(relative.parts) - 1:
                state = state_for_directory(ancestor, state)
                states[str(ancestor)] = state
                continue
            if stat.S_ISDIR(metadata.st_mode):
                subtree = _walk_tree(path, state, root=source)
                files.extend(subtree.files)
                file_count += subtree.file_count
                total_bytes += subtree.total_bytes
                applied.extend(subtree.applied)
            elif component != BKPIGNORE_FILENAME:
                if stat.S_ISREG(metadata.st_mode):
                    file_count += 1
                    total_bytes += metadata.st_size
                    files.append(path)
                elif stat.S_ISLNK(metadata.st_mode):
                    files.append(path)
    rules = list(dict.fromkeys([*_collect_applied(states), *applied]))
    return WalkResult(files, total_bytes, rules, file_count), missing

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

import click
from buvis.pybase.adapters import console
from buvis.pybase.configuration import buvis_options
from buvis.pybase.result import FatalError

from backup.settings import BackupSettings

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from collections.abc import Iterable

    from backup.config import BackupConfig, BackupInstance
    from backup.step_result import StepResult


def _report_step(step: StepResult) -> None:
    if step.skipped:
        console.warning(step.message or f"{step.label} skipped")
    elif step.success:
        console.success(step.message or f"{step.label} archived")
    else:
        console.failure(step.message or f"{step.label} failed")


def _report_steps(steps: Iterable[StepResult], *, dry_run: bool = False) -> bool:
    """Render every step (success and failure) and report whether any failed.

    All steps are rendered before the caller acts on the return, so the user
    sees every failure — the CLI must not stop at the first one. Returns ``True``
    when at least one step failed, so the CLI layer can exit nonzero (a cron job
    treating an incomplete backup as success is the bug this closes).
    """
    archived = skipped = failed = 0
    for step in steps:
        _report_step(step)
        if not step.success:
            failed += 1
        elif step.skipped:
            skipped += 1
        else:
            archived += 1
    verb = "previewed" if dry_run else "archived"
    console.info(f"{verb} {archived}, skipped {skipped}, failed {failed}")
    return failed > 0


def _parse_only(only: tuple[str, ...]) -> set[str]:
    names: set[str] = set()
    for item in only:
        names.update(part.strip() for part in item.split(",") if part.strip())
    return names


def _describe(name: str, instance: BackupInstance) -> str:
    tags = f" [tags: {', '.join(instance.tags)}]" if instance.tags else ""
    return f"{instance.order:>4}  {name}  (use:{instance.use}){tags}"


def _apply_overrides(instance: BackupInstance, source: str, out: str) -> BackupInstance:
    """Return a copy of ``instance`` with ``source`` / ``out`` overridden in ``with_``.

    A non-empty flag value replaces the instance's configured value for a
    one-shot run; an empty value leaves the config value untouched (flag wins
    over config). The frozen model is copied rather than mutated.
    """
    merged = dict(instance.with_)
    if source:
        merged["source"] = source
    if out:
        merged["out"] = out
    return instance.model_copy(update={"with_": merged})


def _override_selected(
    plan: list[tuple[str, BackupInstance]], source: str, out: str
) -> list[tuple[str, BackupInstance]]:
    if not (source or out):
        return plan
    if len(plan) != 1:
        console.failure(
            f"--source/--out require exactly one selected instance (via --only); {len(plan)} selected",
        )
        raise SystemExit(1)
    name, instance = plan[0]
    return [(name, _apply_overrides(instance, source, out))]


def _list_instances(plan: list[tuple[str, BackupInstance]]) -> None:
    if not plan:
        console.info("no configured instances")
    else:
        for name, instance in plan:
            console.info(_describe(name, instance))


def _load_config(ctx: click.Context) -> BackupConfig | None:
    from backup.config import load_config

    # Honour the same --config / --config-dir the buvis_options wrapper resolved
    # settings from, so the backup PLAN and BackupSettings come from ONE source.
    # The wrapper publishes the raw selection on ctx.obj (None when unset); pass
    # it through so `backup --config FILE` runs the plan from FILE and
    # `--config-dir DIR` discovers it under DIR. (PRD 00084 closed the split that
    # was deferred from PR #179.)
    obj = ctx.obj or {}
    config_dir = obj.get("config_dir")
    config_path = obj.get("config_path")
    try:
        return load_config(config_dir=config_dir, config_path=config_path)
    except FatalError as exc:
        console.panic(str(exc))
        return None


def _show_excludes(cfg: BackupConfig, instance_name: str, for_path: str) -> bool:
    """Print the resolved exclude set for ``instance_name`` under ``--for`` path.

    Renders the instance exclude set (after inheritance, removals and additions)
    and, when ``for_path`` is given, the ``.bkpignore`` add / ``!``-unignore
    rules effective under that path — resolved with the same layering the
    archive walk uses. Writes no archive. Without ``--for`` prints the instance
    set only and notes that path-dependent ``.bkpignore`` rules are omitted.

    Returns ``True`` on a terminal validation failure (unknown instance, or an
    instance with no source) so the CLI layer can exit nonzero — a typo like
    ``backup --show-excludes typo`` must not look like a successful inspection
    to a script.
    """
    from pathlib import Path

    from backup.config import effective_excludes
    from backup.shared.bkpignore import ExcludeState, resolve_state_for_path

    instance = cfg.instances.get(instance_name)
    if instance is None:
        console.failure(f"unknown instance '{instance_name}'")
        return True

    excludes = effective_excludes(cfg, instance)
    console.info(f"resolved excludes for '{instance_name}':")
    for pattern in excludes:
        console.info(f"  {pattern}")

    if not for_path:
        console.info("(.bkpignore rules omitted — path-dependent; pass --for <path> to resolve them)")
        return False

    source_raw = instance.with_.get("source")
    if not isinstance(source_raw, str) or not source_raw:
        console.failure(f"instance '{instance_name}' has no source configured")
        return True

    source = Path(source_raw).expanduser()
    target = Path(for_path).expanduser()
    base_state = ExcludeState(base_excludes=frozenset(excludes))
    state = resolve_state_for_path(source, base_state, target)

    console.info(f".bkpignore rules effective under {target}:")
    if state.applied:
        for rule in state.applied:
            console.info(f"  {rule}")
    else:
        console.info("  none")
    return False


def _select_plan(
    cfg: BackupConfig,
    plan: list[tuple[str, BackupInstance]],
    only: tuple[str, ...],
    tags: tuple[str, ...],
) -> tuple[list[tuple[str, BackupInstance]], bool]:
    """Narrow ``plan`` by ``--only`` names and ``--tag`` tags, reporting skips via console.

    Returns the narrowed plan plus a flag that is ``True`` when any requested
    ``--only`` name was unknown to the config. Valid names still run (the caller
    executes whatever survived), but the flag lets the CLI exit nonzero so a typo
    that leaves an empty or reduced plan cannot make a scheduled backup silently

    """
    had_unknown = False
    only_names = _parse_only(only)
    if only_names:
        selected_names = {name for name, _ in plan}
        for requested in sorted(only_names):
            if requested not in cfg.instances:
                console.failure(f"unknown instance '{requested}', skipping")
                had_unknown = True
            elif requested not in selected_names:
                console.info(f"'{requested}' is disabled, skipping")
        plan = [(name, instance) for name, instance in plan if name in only_names]

    if tags:
        wanted = set(tags)
        plan = [(name, instance) for name, instance in plan if wanted & set(instance.tags)]

    return plan, had_unknown


def _run_plan(cfg: BackupConfig, plan: list[tuple[str, BackupInstance]], *, dry_run: bool, plan_only: bool) -> bool:
    """Run the selected plan, rendering every step; return whether any failed.

    Rendering all steps before returning means the user sees every failure (the
    CLI must not stop at the first). Returns ``True`` if any step failed so the
    caller can exit nonzero — a cron job treating an incomplete backup as success
    is the bug this closes. A ``FatalError`` from the runner is surfaced via
    ``console.panic`` (which exits).
    """
    from backup.runner import Runner

    try:
        runner = Runner(cfg, dry_run=dry_run)
        if plan_only:
            entries = runner.plan(plan)
            for entry in entries:
                message = f"{entry.label}  {entry.status}  {entry.source} -> {entry.out}"
                if entry.reason:
                    message += f"  ({entry.reason})"
                if entry.replaces:
                    message += "  [replaces existing]"
                console.info(message)
            return any(entry.status == "fail" for entry in entries)
        return _report_steps(runner.run(plan), dry_run=dry_run)
    except FatalError as exc:
        console.panic(str(exc))
        return True  # unreachable: panic exits, but keeps the type honest


@click.command(help="Run configured backup archives")
@click.option("--only", multiple=True, help="Run only these instance names (comma-separated or repeated).")
@click.option("--tag", "tags", multiple=True, help="Run only instances carrying one of these tags.")
@click.option("--list", "list_plan", is_flag=True, help="Print the configured instances and exit.")
@click.option("--plan", "plan_only", is_flag=True, help="Print the selected archive plan without walking sources.")
@click.option("--dry-run", is_flag=True, help="Walk and report what would be archived without writing it.")
@click.option("--source", default="", help="Override the single selected instance's source for this run.")
@click.option("--out", default="", help="Override the single selected instance's out path for this run.")
@click.option(
    "--show-excludes",
    "show_excludes",
    default="",
    help="Print an instance's resolved exclude set and exit (read-only).",
)
@click.option("--for", "for_path", default="", help="Resolve .bkpignore rules under this path for --show-excludes.")
@buvis_options(settings_class=BackupSettings)
@click.pass_context
def cli(  # noqa: PLR0917  # Click binds one callback arg per CLI option
    ctx: click.Context,
    only: tuple[str, ...],
    tags: tuple[str, ...],
    list_plan: bool,
    plan_only: bool,
    dry_run: bool,
    source: str,
    out: str,
    show_excludes: str,
    for_path: str,
) -> None:
    from backup.config import applicable_instances

    if plan_only and dry_run:
        console.failure("--plan and --dry-run are mutually exclusive")
        raise SystemExit(1)

    # --for only qualifies --show-excludes' read-only inspection; supplied alone
    # it used to be silently ignored while a real backup RAN. Reject it up front.
    if for_path and not show_excludes:
        console.failure("--for requires --show-excludes")
        raise SystemExit(1)

    cfg = _load_config(ctx)
    if cfg is None:
        return

    if show_excludes:
        failed = _show_excludes(cfg, show_excludes, for_path)
        if failed:
            raise SystemExit(1)
        return

    plan = applicable_instances(cfg)
    plan, unknown_only = _select_plan(cfg, plan, only, tags)

    if list_plan:
        _list_instances(plan)
        if unknown_only:
            raise SystemExit(1)
        return

    plan = _override_selected(plan, source, out)
    any_failed = _run_plan(cfg, plan, dry_run=dry_run, plan_only=plan_only)
    # An unknown --only name (typo) must also fail the run, so a scheduled
    # backup can't silently do nothing (or less) after a mistyped selector.
    if any_failed or unknown_only:
        raise SystemExit(1)

from typing import NamedTuple


class ArchiveMeta(NamedTuple):
    """The archive facts a ``tar-archive`` run (or dry-run preview) produces."""

    out_path: str
    file_count: int
    total_bytes: int


class PlanEntry(NamedTuple):
    """One backup plan entry with its preview status and replacement flag."""

    label: str
    source: str
    out: str
    status: str
    reason: str
    replaces: bool


class StepResult:
    """Structured outcome of one capability step.

    ``label`` names the instance, ``success`` is the verdict, and ``message`` is
    a human-readable line the CLI renders via ``console``. ``archive`` carries
    the produced/previewed archive facts, or ``None`` for a step that produces
    no archive. ``skipped`` marks a successful step that has nothing to archive.
    """

    def __init__(
        self: StepResult,
        label: str,
        success: bool,
        message: str = "",
        archive: ArchiveMeta | None = None,
        *,
        skipped: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        self.label = label
        self.success = success
        self.message = message
        self.archive = archive
        self.skipped = skipped

    @property
    def out_path(self: StepResult) -> str | None:
        return self.archive.out_path if self.archive is not None else None

    @property
    def file_count(self: StepResult) -> int | None:
        return self.archive.file_count if self.archive is not None else None

    @property
    def total_bytes(self: StepResult) -> int | None:
        return self.archive.total_bytes if self.archive is not None else None

@runtime_checkable
class Capability(Protocol):
    """A built-in, code-owned backup capability referenced from config by name.

    ``inputs`` declares the accepted ``with:`` keys mapped to their default
    values, so ``load_config`` can reject unknown inputs. ``run`` executes the
    capability and yields one :class:`StepResult` per reported step. A capability
    may raise :class:`buvis.pybase.result.FatalError` for an unrecoverable
    precondition; any other exception is caught by the runner and turned into a
    failed step.
    """

    @property
    def inputs(self: Capability) -> Mapping[str, object]: ...

    def plan(self: Capability, **kwargs: object) -> PlanEntry: ...

    def run(self: Capability, **kwargs: object) -> Iterator[StepResult]: ...

   215	def _reject_out_inside_source(label: str, source: Path, out: Path) -> StepResult | None:
   216	    """Reject an ``out`` path that lands inside the ``source`` tree.
   217	
   218	    An ``out`` under ``source`` makes each run re-archive the previous run's
   219	    archive (unbounded recursive growth). ``out`` may not exist yet, so its
   220	    PARENT is resolved (which does exist — a stamp only expands the basename) and
   221	    the name rejoined, giving a real absolute path to test for containment
   222	    against the resolved source. Returns a failed :class:`StepResult` when ``out``
   223	    is inside ``source`` (the caller yields it and returns before walking),
   224	    otherwise ``None``.
   225	    """
   226	    source_resolved = source.resolve()
   227	    out_resolved = out.parent.resolve() / out.name
   228	    if out_resolved == source_resolved or source_resolved in out_resolved.parents:
   229	        return StepResult(
   230	            label,
   231	            success=False,
   232	            message=(f"out path {out} is inside source {source}; choose an out path outside the backup source"),
   233	        )
   234	    return None

   237	def _normalize_items(source: Path, items: tuple[str, ...]) -> list[Path]:
   238	    """Validate literal item paths and remove duplicate selected subtrees."""
   239	    if not items:
   240	        raise ValueError("items must not be empty")
   241	    selected: list[Path] = []
   242	    for item in items:
   243	        relative = Path(os.path.normpath(item))
   244	        if not item or relative.is_absolute() or relative == Path(".") or relative.parts[0].startswith(".."):

   246	        for parent in reversed(relative.parents):
   247	            if parent != Path(".") and (source / parent).is_symlink():
   248	                raise ValueError(f"item '{item}' passes through symlink '{parent.as_posix()}'")
   249	        if relative not in selected and not any(parent in selected for parent in relative.parents):
   250	            selected = [path for path in selected if relative not in path.parents]
   251	            selected.append(relative)
   252	    return selected

   255	def _select_items(source: Path, base_state: ExcludeState, selected: list[Path]) -> tuple[WalkResult, list[str]]:
   256	    """Select bundle members using source-relative excludes and ancestor rules."""
   257	    files: list[Path] = []
   258	    missing: list[str] = []
   259	    total_bytes = file_count = 0
   260	    states: dict[str, ExcludeState] = {str(source): state_for_directory(source, base_state)}
   261	    applied: list[str] = []
   262	    for relative in selected:
   263	        path = source / relative
   264	        if not os.path.lexists(path):
   265	            missing.append(relative.as_posix())
   266	            continue
   267	        metadata = path.lstat()
   268	        state = states[str(source)]
   269	        for index, component in enumerate(relative.parts):
   270	            ancestor = source.joinpath(*relative.parts[: index + 1])
   271	            relpath = ancestor.relative_to(source).as_posix()
   272	            if state.is_excluded(component, relpath):
   273	                break
   274	            if index < len(relative.parts) - 1:
   275	                state = state_for_directory(ancestor, state)
   276	                states[str(ancestor)] = state
   277	                continue
   278	            if stat.S_ISDIR(metadata.st_mode):
   279	                subtree = _walk_tree(path, state, root=source)
   280	                files.extend(subtree.files)
   281	                file_count += subtree.file_count
   282	                total_bytes += subtree.total_bytes
   283	                applied.extend(subtree.applied)
   284	            elif component != BKPIGNORE_FILENAME:
   285	                if stat.S_ISREG(metadata.st_mode):
   286	                    file_count += 1
   287	                    total_bytes += metadata.st_size
   288	                    files.append(path)
   289	                elif stat.S_ISLNK(metadata.st_mode):
   290	                    files.append(path)

   295	def _walk_tree(source: Path, base_state: ExcludeState, *, root: Path | None = None) -> WalkResult:
   296	    """Walk ``source`` top-down, applying global excludes + path-scoped ``.bkpignore``.
   297

   300	    pruned from further descent; surviving regular files are collected.

   315	        # directory, and an empty source tree's own `src/` entry, would vanish on
   316	        # restore, unlike the former `tar -C ... source`.
   317	        dirs.append(Path(dirpath))
   318	
   319	        kept_dirs: list[str] = []
   320	        for dirname in dirnames:
   321	            child = os.path.join(dirpath, dirname)
   322	            relpath = os.path.relpath(child, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
   323	            if state.is_excluded(dirname, relpath):
   324	                continue
   325	            # A directory symlink: os.walk (followlinks=False) will not descend
   326	            # it, and we must NOT read <link>/.bkpignore (it may point outside
   327	            # the source tree) — so it stays out of kept_dirs. But the link
   328	            # ITSELF is archived as a non-recursive symlink member, so restoring
   329	            # preserves it (the former tar backup kept symlinks). tarfile /
   330	            # system tar store a symlink as a link without following it.
   331	            if os.path.islink(child):
   332	                symlinks.append(Path(child))
   333	                continue
   334	            states[child] = state_for_directory(Path(child), state)
   335	            kept_dirs.append(dirname)
   336	        dirnames[:] = kept_dirs
   337	
   338	        for filename in filenames:
   339	            if filename == BKPIGNORE_FILENAME:
   340	                continue
   341	            file_path = Path(dirpath) / filename
   342	            relpath = os.path.relpath(file_path, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
   343	            if state.is_excluded(filename, relpath):
   344	                continue
   345	            # Archive a symlink as the link itself (not its target), matching the
   346	            # former tar backup — but never stat() it (that follows the link and
   347	            # a broken link would raise); a link contributes 0 input bytes.
   348	            if file_path.is_symlink():
   349	                symlinks.append(file_path)
   350	                continue
   351	            if not file_path.is_file():
   352	                continue
   353	            files.append(file_path)
   354	            # No suppression: a file we selected but cannot stat is a real error
   355	            # for an archiver, not a 0-byte undercount. The runner turns the
   356	            # propagated OSError into a failed step.
   357	            total_bytes += file_path.stat().st_size

   359	    return WalkResult(
   360	        files=[*dirs, *files, *symlinks],
   361	        total_bytes=total_bytes,

   363	        file_count=len(files),

   367	def _raise_walk_error(error: OSError) -> None:

   371	    partial archive reported as success. Re-raising lets the runner's
   372	    ``except Exception -> StepResult(success=False)`` turn it into a failed step.

   377	def _collect_applied(states: dict[str, ExcludeState]) -> list[str]:

   380	    for state in states.values():
   381	        for rule in state.applied:
   382	            if rule not in seen:

   387	def _write_archive(out: Path, arcbase: Path, files: Iterable[Path]) -> None:
   388	    """Stream a ``w:gz`` tarball of ``files`` to ``out`` atomically, ``chmod 600``.
   389	
   390	    Replicates ``pybase.filesystem.atomic_write``'s tempfile + fsync +
   391	    ``os.replace`` guarantee, but streams tar output straight into the temp file
   392	    (a large tarball must never be built in memory, which the byte-oriented
   393	    ``atomic_write_bytes`` would require). Archive names are stored relative to
   394	    ``arcbase``: the source's parent for whole trees, or the source itself for
   395	    selected items.
   396	    """
   397	    fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=out.name + ".", suffix=".tmp", dir=str(out.parent))
   398	    tmp_path = Path(tmp_name)
   399	    try:
   400	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as raw:
   401	            os.fchmod(fd, _ARCHIVE_MODE)
   402	            with tarfile.open(fileobj=raw, mode="w:gz") as tar:
   403	                for file_path in files:
   404	                    arcname = file_path.relative_to(arcbase)
   405	                    tar.add(str(file_path), arcname=str(arcname), recursive=False)
   406	            raw.flush()
   407	            os.fsync(raw.fileno())
   408	        os.replace(tmp_path, out)
   409	    except BaseException:
   410	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
   411	            tmp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
   412	        raise

   414	
   415	def _write_archive_system_tar(out: Path, arcbase: Path, files: Iterable[Path]) -> str | None:
   416	    """Archive ``files`` via system ``tar --null -T -``, atomically, ``chmod 600``.
   417	
   418	    Python still owns selection: ``files`` is the exact include list the walk
   419	    produced (surviving directories, files, and symlinks — so ``.bkpignore``
   420	    path-scoping and empty-directory preservation hold). The paths, relative
   421	    to ``arcbase``, are joined with NUL bytes and streamed to
   422	    ``tar -C <arcbase> --no-recursion --null -T - -czf <tmp>`` on stdin.
   423	    ``--no-recursion`` keeps the filtered list authoritative — a listed directory
   424	    is archived as a bare entry, not re-expanded (which would re-add contents the
   425	    walk excluded). NUL delimiting
   426	    (both GNU tar and macOS bsdtar support ``--null``) means a filename
   427	    containing a newline can never split into an extra ``-T`` line and inject an
   428	    outside/absolute path. The gzip output lands in a sibling temp file, is
   429	    ``fsync``ed and ``chmod 600``ed, then ``os.replace``d into ``out``,
   430	    preserving the Python engine's atomicity and durability guarantee.
   431	
   432	    Returns:
   433	        ``None`` when the archive was written successfully; otherwise a short
   434	        reason string so the caller can fall back to the Python engine and note
   435	        why. A partial temp archive is always cleaned up.
   436	    """
   437	    tar_bin = shutil.which("tar")
   438	    if tar_bin is None:
   439	        return "tar not found on PATH"
   440	
   441	    fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=out.name + ".", suffix=".tmp", dir=str(out.parent))
   442	    os.close(fd)
   443	    tmp_path = Path(tmp_name)
   444	    # NUL-delimited list on stdin: a NUL cannot occur in a POSIX path component,
   445	    # so no filename (even one containing a newline) can inject an extra entry.
   446	    filelist = b"".join(os.fsencode(file_path.relative_to(arcbase)) + b"\0" for file_path in files)
   447	    try:
   448	        # bsdtar (macOS) otherwise stores AppleDouble (``._name``) metadata
   449	        # members that the Python engine never produces; COPYFILE_DISABLE
   450	        # suppresses them and is a no-op for GNU tar on Linux.
   451	        env = {**os.environ, "COPYFILE_DISABLE": "1"}
   452	        completed = subprocess.run(
   453	            [tar_bin, "-C", str(arcbase), "--no-recursion", "--null", "-czf", str(tmp_path), "-T", "-"],
   454	            input=filelist,
   455	            capture_output=True,
   456	            check=False,
   457	            env=env,
   458	        )
   459	        if completed.returncode != 0:
   460	            stderr = completed.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace").strip().splitlines()
   461	            detail = stderr[-1] if stderr else f"exit {completed.returncode}"
   462	            return f"tar exited {completed.returncode}: {detail}"
   463	        # Match the Python engine's durability: fsync the finished temp archive
   464	        # before atomically swapping it into place.
   465	        archive_fd = os.open(str(tmp_path), os.O_RDONLY)
   466	        try:
   467	            os.fsync(archive_fd)
   468	        finally:
   469	            os.close(archive_fd)
   470	        os.chmod(tmp_path, _ARCHIVE_MODE)
   471	        os.replace(tmp_path, out)
   472	    except OSError as exc:
   473	        return f"tar invocation failed: {exc}"
   474	    finally:
   475	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
   476	            tmp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
   477	    return None

   480	def _parse_inputs(kwargs: Mapping[str, object]) -> tuple[str, str, str, str, datetime | None]:
   481	    """Parse label, engine, raw source/out and ``now``; an empty engine means the python engine."""
   482	    return (
   483	        _require_str(kwargs, "label", default="tar-archive"),
   484	        _require_str(kwargs, "engine", default=_ENGINE_PYTHON) or _ENGINE_PYTHON,
   485	        _require_str(kwargs, "source"),
   486	        _require_str(kwargs, "out"),
   487	        cast("datetime | None", kwargs.get("now")),
   488	    )

   491	def _missing_input(source_raw: str, out_raw: str) -> str:
   492	    """Return the missing-input message, or ``""`` when both source and out are set."""
   493	    if not source_raw:
   494	        return "no source configured"
   495	    return "" if out_raw else "no out path configured"

   497	
   498	def _resolve_paths(source_raw: str, out_raw: str, now: datetime | None) -> tuple[Path, Path]:
   499	    # Normalize `.`/`..` LEXICALLY (os.path.normpath, not resolve()) before
   500	    # walking: a source like `parent/child/..` would otherwise be walked as
   501	    # given and produce member names like `..` / `../child` (an unsafe
   502	    # archive that also breaks the documented source-name prefix). normpath
   503	    # collapses the segments without following symlinks, so the
   504	    # symlink-confinement guarantee is untouched.
   505	    source = Path(os.path.normpath(Path(source_raw).expanduser()))
   506	    return source, Path(_expand_stamp(out_raw, now)).expanduser()
   507

   509	def _require_str(kwargs: Mapping[str, object], key: str, *, default: str = "") -> str:
   510	    value = kwargs.get(key, default)
   511	    return value if isinstance(value, str) else default
   512	
   513	
   514	def _expand_stamp(pattern: str, now: datetime | None = None) -> str:
   515	    """Expand ``strftime`` codes in an ``out`` pattern against the supplied or current time.
   516	
   517	    A pattern like ``git-src-%Y%m%d-%H%M%S.tar.gz`` becomes a timestamped name
   518	    at archive time, reproducing the wrapped script's ``date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S``
   519	    behaviour. A pattern with no ``%`` codes is returned unchanged.
   520	    """
   521	    if "%" not in pattern:
   522	        return pattern
   523	    return (now if now is not None else datetime.now()).strftime(pattern)
   524

   526	def _as_str_tuple(value: object) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   527	    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
   528	        return tuple(str(item) for item in value)
   529	    return ()
